mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (for registration under the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance or Business Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: certify by the Hong Kong High Court Authentication Service before submission in China for UBO registration under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3; China has acceded to the Apostille Convention effective November 7, 2023, so apostille is the exclusive path and consular legalization must not be added

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: obtain certified true copy from Companies Registry, then apostille through Hong Kong High Court; no consular legalization by the Chinese Embassy in Hong Kong

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the Chinese FIP general partner and legalization signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or general partner of the offshore parent or Hong Kong holding entity, notarized by a Hong Kong notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarization by authorized Hong Kong notary followed by apostille at the High Court; consular legalization is inapplicable because Hong Kong and Mainland China are both within the Apostille Convention's application scope for cross-border instruments

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Limited Partnership Agreement) of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered law firm or formation agent, executed by all partners, filed with the Hong Kong Companies Registry or applicable local registration authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarized copy of the executed partnership agreement, followed by apostille through the Hong Kong High Court Authentication Service; no sequential consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the general partner's and partners' banking history and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: each bank's signature notarized, then apostilled by the competent authority of the bank's jurisdiction if that jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; if the bank is located in a non-member state, use consular legalization at the Chinese embassy/consulate exclusively

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, authorized representatives, general partners, and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Customs and Excise Department sanctions lists, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list before any formation step. Each individual and entity must undergo enhanced due diligence if flagged as a Politically Exposed Person, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring, and 10-year record retention under Cap. 615. Negative news and adverse media checks must be completed in both English and Chinese language sources, with re-screening at every material change and at least quarterly refresh.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Search and Name Search on the Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS); for foreign-invested partnership establishment in Mainland China, National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (国家企业信用信息公示系统) and provincial Market Supervision Administration one-stop name clearance portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For the Hong Kong entity, the English name must not be identical or too similar to an existing registered company or LPF; the Chinese name must have a corresponding transliteration that is not misleading. For the Mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership, the name must consist of four tiers: administrative division + unique name + industry characteristic + organization form (e.g., Shenzhen + [selected name] + Organic Matcha Powder Trading + Partnership Enterprise). Chinese characters must be used, with pinyin transliteration only for non-Chinese partner names; foreign-language transliteration of the entity name is not accepted as a substitute in the State Administration for Market Regulation registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Group (where implying cross-industry conglomerate without approval)
Limited (unless registered as a limited partnership)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must obtain the written rejection notice from the Market Supervision Administration or Companies Registry, stating the statutory ground and conflicting registered name. Within 15 working days of the rejection, the applicant must file a formal administrative reconsideration with the next-higher Market Supervision Administration or with the Companies Registry's Standing Committee on Company Names, attaching the proposed name, the rejection notice, evidence of the applicant's lawful business scope, and a legal argument that the proposed name is distinguishable, non-deceptive, and not likely to cause confusion. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within six months, or, for Hong Kong registry decisions, apply for judicial review within three months. The applicant may simultaneously reserve a backup name and refile without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible as the sole registered address for the Mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership because the State Administration for Market Regulation and the municipal tax authority require a physical business premises within the registered administrative district, evidenced by a lease agreement or property ownership certificate, and the tax authority's collection and management system will flag a mailbox address as low-substance for VAT invoice issuance and preferential pass-through treatment. For the Hong Kong vehicle, a licensed corporate service provider's registered office address is acceptable for Companies Registry compliance, but Hong Kong Inland Revenue and banks will deny substantial business presence and Hong Kong profits tax treaty benefits if there is no local office, local director, accounting records, and operating activity in Hong Kong. The recommended compliant structure is a physical serviced office in Hong Kong plus a registered leased office in the Mainland pilot free-trade zone or local municipality, with utility bills, lease stamps, and employment records of at least one local general staff member retained onsite.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered address matches lease; (2) signboard bearing approved Chinese name posted at entrance; (3) original lease, utility bills, and property ownership or sublease approval available; (4) statutory books, partnership agreement, UBO register, and tax registration certificates maintained; (5) staff present during business hours; (6) business correspondence and invoices issued from the address; (7) inventory or warehouse documentation consistent with matcha powder trade volume. Risk quantification: municipal market supervision bureaus conduct targeted on-site inspections in approximately 18 percent of newly registered partnerships in the food and agricultural products distribution sector within the first 12 months; tax authorities conduct unannounced visits in approximately 10 percent of entities applying for pass-through or small-scale taxpayer status; the combined likelihood of at least one physical inspection in the first year is estimated at 28 percent. Failure to pass inspection may result in registration revocation, name cancellation, tax blacklisting, and denial of UBO filing acceptance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the Laws of Hong Kong SAR, including sections 67-71 (incorporation by registration), section 112 (registered office), section 124 (appointment of directors), sections 373-376 (financial statements), and the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) sections 4-7 for partnership registration; the Foreign-Invested Partnership is structured as a registered limited partnership under Cap. 37, read together with the Companies Ordinance where corporate general partner requirements apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; for foreign-invested partnership registration, the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department is the parallel authority for business registration, and where the partnership uses a corporate general partner, the Companies Registry remains the registration authority for that corporate vehicle.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP1) under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) together with a Statement of Particulars; where a corporate general partner is incorporated, the incorporation instrument is the Incorporation Form (NNC1) and Articles of Association filed under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong SAR imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for limited partnerships or foreign-invested partnerships. The partners may agree on capital contributions by partnership agreement without any statutory escrow or blocked account. For AML and banking counterparty due diligence purposes, the bank may internally require a minimum initial deposit, but this is not a statutory incorporation requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE PARTNERSHIP MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE AND CORPORATE GENERAL PARTNER OF [●] FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (the “Partnership”), DULY CONVENED AND HELD ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT [ADDRESS], HONG KONG SAR. PRESENT: The undersigned partners, being the general partner [●] and the limited partners [●], together holding more than 75% of the initial capital commitments and constituting a quorum in accordance with the Partnership Agreement, hereby resolve as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND CAPITAL COMMITMENTS: RESOLVED that the initial capital commitments of the partners, in the aggregate amount of USD [●] (or its equivalent in HKD), be and are hereby approved, and the general partner be and is hereby authorized to open, operate, and maintain one or more bank accounts in the name of the Partnership, with authority to execute all account opening forms, mandates, and electronic banking agreements. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Partnership in Hong Kong shall be situated at [●], being a place within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and the general partner is authorized to file the prescribed notice with the Companies Registry and to notify the Inland Revenue Department, and to receive and respond to all statutory correspondence at such address. 3. BUSINESS SCOPE: RESOLVED that the Partnership shall engage solely in the lawful business of cross-border procurement, distribution, and wholesale trade of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder, falling under ISIC 4631 and NAICS 424490, and the general partner shall ensure no activity is undertaken that would require licensing under the Import and Export Ordinance without the necessary permit. 6. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR, Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS), and the Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the ICRIS platform for the proposed English and optional Chinese name of the foreign-invested partnership, ensuring the name does not exceed 100 characters including spaces and suffixes. Reserve the name for a six-month block by filing a Name Reservation application in the prescribed form via the Companies Registry's e-filing portal. If the name contains a sensitive expression such as 'bank,' 'trust,' or 'insurance,' obtain prior written consent from the relevant authority. If a corporate general partner is used, verify its name is valid and in good standing. Should the search reveal a conflicting name, file a fresh reservation for an alternative name or apply for a direction from the Companies Registry to overcome the conflict, ensuring any defect is cured within 14 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name in English and Chinese (if desired)
Certificate of Incorporation of the corporate general partner (if any), including its current name search result
Identity documents of the general partner and all limited partners (passport copies or corporate registry extracts)
Certificate of Good Standing for the corporate general partner if registered outside Hong Kong
Written consent letters for any sensitive name expressions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, immediately file a revised name reservation with a new proposed name, preserving fee credits if permitted. In case of a formal requisition from the Companies Registry, respond in writing within 20 business days with revised consent letters, an alternative name, or a written undertaking to adopt an alternative name, and pay the applicable fee for releasing the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement and Capital Contribution Statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel and notarial professionals authorized in Hong Kong; execution by all partners on the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft a comprehensive partnership agreement defining the general partner, limited partners, capital commitments, profit sharing, management powers, transfer restrictions, dissolution triggers, and the governing law of Hong Kong SAR. The agreement must include a business scope clause strictly limiting the Partnership to wholesale distribution of organic matcha powder, prohibiting activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, Import and Export Ordinance, or Food Safety Ordinance unless separately licensed. Each partner must execute the agreement, with signatures notarially attested where required by a partner's home jurisdiction or the account opening bank. Prepare the capital contribution schedule and banking mandate schedule, then stamp the agreement under the Stamp Duty Ordinance if chargeable; otherwise, obtain a certificate of non-chargeability. Maintain a certified copy of the executed agreement for presentation to the Companies Registry and banks.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement executed by all partners
Capital contribution statement specifying each partner's amount and currency
Banking mandate schedule with signatory authority limits
Notarially apostilled power of attorney for any partner acting by representative
Certificate of Incumbency or legal opinion for any corporate partner
Stamp duty self-assessment form and payment evidence (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the stamp office or Companies Registry queries execution or capital particulars, submit a revised clean execution version with a supplemental partner resolution ratifying the corrections. If the Registry requires proof of the corporate general partner's capacity, obtain a certified certificate of good standing and legal opinion from the general partner's home jurisdiction and re-file within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Limited Partnership and Application for Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (Limited Partnerships Registry Section) and Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP1 to the Companies Registry together with the prescribed fee, the executed partnership agreement, the capital contribution statement, and the registered office address in Hong Kong. The form must state the partnership name, nature of business as wholesale trade of matcha and other food products, registered office, partnership term, and full particulars of all partners with the general partner clearly designated. Upon approval, the Companies Registry will issue the Certificate of Registration of a Limited Partnership. Immediately thereafter, file the application for Business Registration with the Business Registration Office using Form IRBR1, within one month of commencing business. For cross-border procurement not involving physical import into Hong Kong, no import/export license is required, but the partnership must maintain records demonstrating the pure agency or paper trade model. If goods physically enter Hong Kong, apply for food importer registration as set out in Step 5. The Registry may issue a notice of defects; the applicant must file an amended LP1 and pay the relevant late filing fee, if any, within 14 days.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by the general partner
Executed partnership agreement
Registered office lease or landlord consent letter
Certificate of Incorporation of corporate general partner (if applicable)
Identity documents of all partners
Certificate of Incumbency of the corporate general partner
Business Registration application Form IRBR1
Notice to Commissioner of Inland Revenue of commencement of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition or if the Business Registration Office suspends the certificate, provide a written reply within 21 days, pay the prorated business registration fee and levy, and file a revised LP1 with the actual commencement date. If the Registry rules that a limited partnership cannot be used and directs incorporation of a company, dissolve the partnership and re-route the name reservation to a new company, preserving fee credits if permitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Filing, Bank Account Activation, and Governance Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and the chosen licensed bank in Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receiving the Certificate of Registration and Business Registration Certificate, update the registered office file and deliver all certificates to the designated representative. Open a partnership bank account at a licensed bank by presenting the certificate of registration, Business Registration Certificate, partnership agreement, minutes of the first partnership committee meeting, resolution of the general partner, ultimate beneficial ownership declarations, and source of funds statements. After the account is activated, receive the partners' capital contributions and issue contribution receipts. File all statutory notifications with the Inland Revenue Department, including any change of registered office within 15 days. Adopt a statutory register listing each partner's name, address, and capital contribution, and retain minutes of the inaugural management meeting approving the banking signatories. If the bank requires further AML review, provide an apostilled certificate of good standing for each non-Hong Kong partner together with a formal explanation of the Partnership's beneficial ownership chain.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement
Minutes of the First Partnership Management Meeting and First Board Resolution
Capital contribution receipts and bank opening forms
Ultimate beneficial ownership statement for the limited partnership
Certified passport copies and address proofs for all partners
Bank reference letters if requested by the account opening bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank holds the account pending further AML review, submit a statutory declaration from the general partner along with certified capital contribution ledger evidence and corporate source-of-funds records. If the Inland Revenue Department queries the commencement date, provide a corrected Business Registration Certificate after conforming the date. If the Companies Registry suspends for failure to file an annual return, file the late return, pay the statutory penalty multiplier, and obtain reinstatement confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory Notification for Food Product Trade and Compliance Calendar Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Customs and Excise Department, and Trade and Industry Department of Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assess whether the Partnership's activity involves the physical importation of matcha powder into Hong Kong. If goods are physically imported and re-exported, register as a Food Importer/Exporter with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department and maintain all import/export permits. If goods are warehoused, obtain a Food Storage Permit and a Fire Safety Certificate from the Fire Services Department. If the trade is pure cross-border flow without goods entering Hong Kong, no FEHD license is mandatory; obtain a written exemption note for bank and record purposes. Maintain a legal register of all permit expiration dates, annual return deadlines, tax deadlines under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and Customs declarations. Preserve all purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations for at least 7 years. If the FEHD queries the matcha's compliance with pesticide residue and heavy metal limits, provide a third-party laboratory analysis certificate and a Certificate of Free Sale from the manufacturer's country of origin.
required_dossiers: Food Importer/Exporter Registration application (if goods physically enter Hong Kong)
Organic matcha certificate of origin and organic certification
Certificate of Free Sale from manufacturer's country of origin
Analysis certificate confirming compliance with pesticide residue and heavy metal standards
Commercial invoices and purchase contracts
Warehouse address and storage permit (if applicable)
Fire services certificate for any warehouse or cold storage facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a permit or registration is deferred or refused, suspend distribution of the affected batch, provide corrected laboratory certificates and labels, and seek written confirmation from the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department. If Customs requires an export declaration, file the declaration online using the customs system, pay the statutory charge, and retain the declaration number with the commercial records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department of Hong Kong SAR; for any physical warehouse or repacking facility, the Buildings Department and Fire Services Department through the One-Stop Integrated Licensing Portal of the Trade and Industry Department
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Importer/Exporter Registration under the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60); Food Storage Permit under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) if warehousing matcha powder in Hong Kong

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department of Hong Kong SAR under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for the current pure trading and cross-border distribution model, as no manufacturing, chemical processing, combustion, or effluent discharge is carried out in Hong Kong. Should a future matcha powder repacking, blending, or packaging facility be established with thresholds triggering Schedule 2 activities, a full EIA report would be required; any smaller facility would require an Environmental Registration or 'Engineering Feasibility Study' under Category 2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure trade. For any future warehousing or repacking activity, comply with the Hong Kong Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311) dust and particulate emission limit of no more than 50 mg/m3 for general non-combustion ventilation exhaust; the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358) trade effluent limits of BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L and suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L for discharge to foul sewers; and the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354) registration as a chemical waste producer for any hazardous wastes such as spent solvents, fluorescent lamps, or chemical cleaning agents, with a special waste handling permit if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Services Department certification is mandatory if the Partnership occupies a warehouse, repacking facility, or any premises where goods are stored in quantities exceeding the thresholds under the Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295). A Fire Safety Certificate or Fire Services Installation Compliance Certificate must be obtained before operation. The Buildings Department must issue structural load approval for racking and storage, and the Labour Department must be notified under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) for any manual handling or forklift operations, requiring a workplace risk assessment and an approved emergency exit plan. For the current pure digital trade operation with no physical facility in Hong Kong, no civil defense clearance is required, but the registered office must maintain clear fire escape routes and general fire safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), accessed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Taxation) online portal; the CN_FIP must register with the STA branch having territorial competence over its registered business address in the PRC. Hong Kong SAR is a separate customs and tax territory; its Inland Revenue Department does not administer VAT/GST, and no Hong Kong VAT/GST registration applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Complete formation at the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which becomes the statutory tax identifier. Step 2: Within 30 days of the business license date, submit the initial tax registration particulars through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau portal or at the competent tax office, including the partnership agreement, SAMR license, legal representative identity documents, registered address proof, and basic bank deposit account certificate. Step 3: Register each foreign non-resident partner for PRC taxpayer identification to the extent a payable or withholding obligation arises; the FIP is a pass-through entity for income tax purposes. Step 4: Receive the electronic tax registration record; the USCC is used as the TIN/VAT number for VAT returns, customs export filings, export tax refunds, e-invoices, and withholding payments. Step 5: Elect or be classified as VAT taxpayer status; the FIP is a small-scale taxpayer until annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, at which time general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory. Step 6: Activate the fully digital e-invoice platform, obtain invoice quota, and receive the anti-fraud digital stamp credentials for real-time invoice clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law; the FIP is statutorily transparent and each partner is taxed on his/her/its allocable share. No hybrid mismatch election is available. The only relevant statutory elections are VAT small-scale versus general taxpayer status and, for general taxpayers, the export tax refund method (tax exemption, credit, and refund).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) in the People's Republic of China; Hong Kong SAR imposes no VAT, GST, or sales tax on the cross-border matcha trade leg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer applies when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; a small-scale taxpayer with monthly taxable sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 qualifies for the statutory VAT exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Golden Tax Phase IV mandates that all Special VAT Invoices be issued through the STA-approved fully digital e-invoice system and transmitted in real time to the tax authority. Newly registered FIPs must use the digital e-invoice platform, maintain digital invoice quotas, and apply anti-fraud digital stamping; printed-only VAT invoices are ineffective for input VAT credit or export tax refund substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Organic matcha powder physically exported from the PRC, including exports to the Hong Kong SAR as a separate customs territory, qualifies for the 0% export VAT rate if: (1) the goods are declared to PRC Customs for export; (2) the FIP has general VAT taxpayer status; (3) the export is supported by a valid overseas sales contract and commercial invoice; (4) the VAT return reports the zero-rated export and related input VAT is recoverable; and (5) the export proceeds are received from the non-resident buyer and repatriated into the PRC within the statutory deadline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document
Commercial invoice with zero-rated VAT annotation
Bank Credit Advice and Inward Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued under SAFE rules
Export tax refund declaration filed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau export tax refund system
Foreign exchange receipt verification log showing repatriation within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and PRC Customs may jointly audit all export zero-rating claims. If the goods were not physically exported, the documents are false or missing, or foreign exchange is not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, the tax authority will claw back the refunded VAT, charge late-payment interest, and impose a penalty of 50% to 500% of the refunded amount under Article 66 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds may arise when the fraudulently obtained refund exceeds RMB 100,000; customs authorities may also confiscate goods and impose fines for false declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) through its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for mainland China; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The regulatory matrix splits between mainland China and Hong Kong SAR. Onshore, RMB is fully convertible for current account trade transactions, but capital account flows remain materially restricted and require SAFE registration, approval, or use of a qualified investor channel. A foreign-invested partnership (CN_FIP) receiving non-resident capital contributions will be classified as direct investment; therefore the remitting partner must use an approved bank integrated with SAFE's FDI-PCI system, obtain a foreign exchange registration certificate, and open a dedicated capital account for the escrow of inbound partnership capital. Once funded, those monies are ring-fenced to the FIP's declared business purpose; use for domestic matcha procurement or operating expenses is allowed only after the bank performs its capital project payment compliance review, and any amendment to partner shareholding, early capital return, or dissolution proceeds needs a separate SAFE filing. Dividend or profit distributions to non-resident partners are treated as current account remittances, yet banks will require audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and corroboration that the distribution is genuine accumulated profit. In contrast, Hong Kong SAR operates under the HKMA's linked exchange rate system with no exchange controls; the HKD is freely convertible, capital flows in and out without SAFE-style approval, and profit remittance is not subject to a separate foreign exchange permit. The practical constraint in Hong Kong is bank KYC: escalating beneficial ownership documentation, source-of-funds verification, and sanctions screening are mandatory. Any CNY settlement executed through Hong Kong must also comply with the offshore CNH clearing mechanisms administered by HKMA and the designated clearing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a mainland China-incorporated FIP, export proceeds from matcha powder sales must be repatriated to a designated domestic foreign exchange bank and are generally subject to a 100% settlement requirement into RMB unless SAFE has approved a specific foreign exchange account retention limit. The standard general-trade collection window is within 90 days from the date of export customs declaration, extendable to 180 days with prior SAFE monitoring registration; the bank reconciles the customs declaration, tax export data, and incoming SWIFT credit. In Hong Kong SAR, there is no statutory export surrender regime; 100% of foreign currency export proceeds may be retained, and those balances can be directly used to settle offshore trade payables without conversion or repatriation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (Shanghai or Shenzhen branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for SAFE-registered FDI / Basic Operational RMB and Forex Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Finance Facility
Capital Escrow Account / CNH and HKD Operational Currency Account
Trade Finance and Documentary Clearing Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: CRITICALLY LOW as the primary treasury rail for mainland China operations; MODERATE as an ancillary collection channel for Hong Kong. offshore digital EMIs without a banking or stored value facility license are legally barred from servicing statutory capital account flows, export proceeds surrender, and capital verification for a mainland FIP, because SAFE requires all foreign exchange receipts and payments to flow through a licensed onshore bank with direct SAFE reporting connectivity. In Hong Kong, HKMA-licensed virtual banks are permissible for basic multi-currency current accounts, but they generally do not underwrite complex trade finance, commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, or sanctions-heavy matcha procurement portfolios. Therefore, the compliance committee should not select an unlicensed fintech EMI as the sole liquidity clearing provider; tier-1 banks must carry the capital escrow, FX settlement, and LC rails, while a licensed HKMA stored value facility may only be used for small value collections if the counterparty insists on a digital wallet.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For mainland China FIP bank onboarding, the legal representative or an appropriately authorized finance officer must attend the bank branch in person with the original business license, partnership agreement, SAFE FDI registration certificate, and a board or partner resolution; a fully remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted for the first capital account. In Hong Kong SAR, at least one authorized signatory or responsible partner must complete an in-person branch interview unless the bank's digital onboarding program allows a video interview supplemented by a notarized power of attorney, a Hong Kong trust or corporate services provider attestation, and certified copies of the partnership deed. Most tier-1 banks require the physical or virtual interview to cover the matcha procurement cycle, expected transaction volume, counterparty geography, source of wealth, and intended use of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership concealment through multi-layer non-resident partners in the FIP, especially where the ultimate principals cannot be readily identified from public filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO chart, certified partnership agreement, register of all partners with scanned passports, FATCA/CRS self-certifications, source-of-wealth statements for each non-resident partner, a legal opinion from a PRC or Hong Kong counsel confirming the FIP's ownership structure, and a written explanation of each partner's commercial role in the organic matcha supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag arising from inconsistent pricing, over-invoicing, or under-invoicing on matcha powder import or export transactions relative to prevailing market benchmarks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A transactional evidence pack covering at least three historical shipments, comprising commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations, bill of lading or airway bill, phytosanitary certificate, organic certification, laboratory analysis, third-party commodity price benchmark reports, and bank payment confirmations to evidence that the goods exist and the price is economically real.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or adverse media linked to counterparties, shipping lines, ports, or partners in jurisdictions subject to OFAC, EU, UN, or mainland Chinese sanction lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A sanctions screening report generated by a reputable screening engine for all partners, beneficial owners, banks, carriers, middlemen, and ultimate buyers; a denied-party list check; a shipping route description with port calls; certificate of origin for the organic matcha; and contractual warranties or supplier undertaking clauses binding counterparties against trading with sanctioned persons or using sanctioned vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the capital actually received through the SWIFT wire and the registered capital or partnership agreement, raising concerns of unlicensed lending or disguised equity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A capital contribution schedule cross-referencing each SWIFT MT103 instruction to the relevant partnership agreement clause, partner board resolutions, source-of-funds bank statements from each contributing partner, the SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate or HKMA CRS filing, and a CPA-issued capital verification report confirming that the received funds are legitimate partnership contributions and not undisclosed loans.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must flowthrough SWIFT MT103 from the contributing partner's bank to the FIP's designated tier-1 account, using clear purpose codes such as 'FDI capital contribution' for mainland SAFE registration or 'equity injection to partnership' for Hong Kong. The routing must include the FIP's business licence number, SAFE foreign exchange registration certificate, the partnership agreement reference, and a fund utilisation schedule describing the matcha procurement project. For mainland onshore use, the receiving bank must perform capital item income payment confirmation, verify the capital contribution against the registered amount, and instruct the auditor to issue a capital verification report. For Hong Kong SAR, no pre-approval is required, but the bank will require the source of funds, partner identification, and CRS self-certification before crediting the escrow account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for matcha powder trade should be executed primarily by SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments where the transaction value is below trade finance thresholds and the counterparty is well known. For larger procurement contracts, the FIP should use irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued by MT700 / MT707, with the beneficiary required to present the organic matcha certificate, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, packing list, and full set of clean bills of lading. Documentary collections (D/P or D/A) may be used for established trade relationships where the FIP wishes to reduce LC confirmation costs; all outbound payments must be supported by underlying purchase orders, invoices, customs declarations, and tax records to demonstrate a genuine goods trade and to avoid the appearance of a shell treasury circuit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla forward FX contracts with a licensed tier-1 bank, limited to no more than the notional value of projected matcha procurement and sales invoices and requiring an underlying trade document or purchase order at trade date.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNH/CNY markets for onshore RMB exposure when the FIP cannot access onshore forwards, strictly documented as a hedge of specific payment obligations and prohibited from creating naked speculative positions.

Cross-currency swaps between HKD, USD, CNH, and RMB applied only to the principal and interest flows of the FIP's underlying trade finance or capital injection, with maturity aligned to the underlying commercial receivable or payable.

Plain-vanilla FX options used sparingly to cap the cost of matcha import payables in RMB, only when the bank confirms that the premium is paid from genuine operating cash flow and that the option is tied to an enforceable underlying trade contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate annual renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the expiry of the existing Business Registration Certificate (typically the registration anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalty of HK$3,000; continued default is an offence with a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and imprisonment of one year. Failure may lead to cancellation of the business registration, triggering administrative strike-off and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for partnerships (Form BIR51) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued usually on the first working day of April; must be filed within one month, or on the extended due date granted by the IRD (typically 30 days from issuance, with possible approved deferrals)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a maximum fine of HK$10,000; upon conviction, an additional fine of HK$10,000 and treble tax undercharged may be imposed. The IRD may raise estimated assessments and initiate collection/distraint action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership annual return (Form LP2) under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the annual return within the prescribed period is an offence punishable on conviction by a fine of HK$2,000. Continued default may expose the partnership to strike-off proceedings initiated by the Registrar, with assets becoming bona vacantia in extreme cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer Return (Form BIR56A and related schedules) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), if the partnership employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 1 April (for payments made in the previous year; extension may be granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An offence punishable by a fine of up to HK$10,000 for each failure; the IRD may also require an employer to file a return. A daily penalty may be ordered by a court.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every Hong Kong-incorporated company is required to have its financial statements audited, irrespective of turnover, assets, or headcount. However, this entity is constituted as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37). There is no statutory requirement in Hong Kong law for a partnership to undergo a certified CPA audit based on balance sheet size, turnover, or number of employees. No quantitative threshold applies. A statutory audit may only be triggered if the partnership is also incorporated as a company (which is not the case), is subject to an alternative regulatory framework (e.g., licensed corporations under the SFO requiring audits under Section 153 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance), or if the partnership agreement/bank covenants impose an audit duty. For this non-licensed cross-border trading partnership, no compulsory audit threshold is reached.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements, if prepared voluntarily or contractually required, should be compiled in accordance with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are closely aligned with IFRS. Hong Kong-incorporated private entities may also apply HKFRS for Private Entities (the SME standard). For tax purposes, partnership accounts should be prepared in a manner consistent with the Inland Revenue Ordinance, typically using HKFRS as the base framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no statutory annual UBO confirmation requirement for a Hong Kong limited partnership. However, any change in the partners, including an assignment, withdrawal, or admission of a partner, must be filed with the Companies Registry within 7 days of the change, and with the Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Office) within 30 days. The partnership must maintain current information on its material controllers for anti-money-laundering purposes, and such records must be accessible to law enforcement. A 30-day reporting window applies for changes to the commercial registration particulars; a 7-day window applies for limited partnership registration particulars.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (analogous to Register of Members)
Register of Capital Contributions, Profit Shares and Distributions
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and General Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 per annum (voluntary, if required by banks or internal governance)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (Hong Kong Profits Tax standard rate for partnerships; the Foreign-Invested Partnership is an unincorporated pass-through; corporations pay 16.5%; two-tier relief charges 7.5% on the first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Offshore-sourced profits exemption under Hong Kong territorial source doctrine; no VAT, capital gains, or dividend withholding tax; substantive matcha trading activities managed in Hong Kong may produce a zero effective rate for qualifying offshore profits; no patent box, but R&D deductions, digitalisation expenses, depreciation/capital allowances, approved charitable donations, and the 8.25% reduced capital component on the first HK$2,000,000 of corporate profits may reduce effective tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 - Profits Tax Return for Partnerships, filed through the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department e-Tax and GovHK electronic tax services portal; audited partnership financial statements and supporting tax schedules must be retained and may be uploaded with the return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The BIR52 must be filed within one month from the date of issue of the return by LRD; e-filing generally receives an automatic extension of up to 14 days, and longer extensions may be granted where audited accounts are not yet available and a tax representative is appointed; the Hong Kong basis period normally ends on 31 March, but the FIP may adopt a 31 December accounting date if approved

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Business Registration Number, Tax File Number, and full correspondence address of the Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sower the overseas partner name and passport/company identification number; confirm whether the non-resident partner is a tax resident of China or another treaty jurisdiction; incomplete identification will trigger AEOI/CRS reporting and possible denial of DTA relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address, principal business activity, and industry code for wholesale distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the actual procurement, quality control, negotiation, invoicing, and risk management location; if the business claims offshore trading profits, the BIR52 narrative must show that core income-generating activities are performed by employees or partners physically in Hong Kong and not by a Chinese supplier or mainland agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period commencement and cessation dates, including the financial statement date and whether the return covers a 12-month period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the Hong Kong basis period with the partnership accounting period; for a non-resident partner with calendar-year accounting, state the different year of assessment and explain any reallocation to avoid double assessment in China and Hong Kong

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per the profit and loss statement before taxation adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all worldwide trading gains from matcha powder sales in the accounts, then make source allocation; do not simply omit mainland-origin resale proceeds from the accounts because the IRD may recharacterise the whole activity as Hong Kong sourced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back adjustment for non-deductible expenses such as domestic private expenses, depreciation, penalties, taxes on profits, and any expenditure not incurred wholly and exclusively in producing assessable profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments must be added back where intercompany purchases of matcha from related Chinese suppliers exceed arm s length prices; a non-resident partner cannot claim inflated cost of goods sold without robust CUP/TNMM evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for capital allowances, approved charitable donations, and losses carried forward from prior periods
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may only offset Hong Kong assessable profits of the same trade; a non-resident partner cannot use mainland tax losses against Hong Kong matcha trading profits unless separately sourced through Hong Kong activities; keep contemporaneous loss schedules to substantiate any claim

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of adjusted assessable profit or loss among each partner under the partnership agreement, with separate statement of Hong Kong-sourced and offshore-sourced shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, allocate profits according to economic substance and authority over decision-making; if the partnership deed is not a genuine commercial agreement, the IRD will reallocate profits under section 22 and impose penalties; a non-resident partner should attach a written source analysis and tax residency certificate for treaty relief

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable excuse exposes the FIP to an estimated assessment under section 59(3) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance; the LRD may impose additional tax of up to treble the undercharged tax plus fines from HK$10,000 to HK$100,000; continuing default may generate daily surcharges; deliberate false statements in Box 1 to Box 6+ attract criminal prosecution under sections 80, 82, and 82A with fines up to HK$50,000 and imprisonment up to three years, plus civil recovery of unpaid tax, arrears interest, and blacklisting of the responsible partner through HK travel restriction mechanisms

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%: Hong Kong does not levy withholding tax on outbound dividends or profit distributions made by a Hong Kong Foreign-Invested Partnership to non-resident partners; the distribution is also exempt from Hong Kong profits tax in the hands of the non-resident partner if sourced outside Hong Kong and not a trading receipt
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Hong Kong imposes no dividend withholding tax, no step-DTA relief is required on the Hong Kong outbound payment. To claim reduced source-state withholding on income paid from China or another treaty partner, the FIP must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the IRD (Form IR1313A), supply a beneficial ownership certificate demonstrating the partner is not a conduit, confirm the partner holds at least 25% of the payer for the 5% China-HK DTA dividend rate, provide a China-HK DTA residence declaration, and document the substantive Hong Kong business activity for the Principal Purpose Test; the claim must be filed with the source-country tax authority before or at the time of the remittance and supporting documents must be kept for at least six years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong statutory WHT on interest is 0% in the absence of a Hong Kong trade; royalties paid to a non-resident may be deemed Hong Kong-sourced profits under section 15(1)(a)/(b) and, where no permanent establishment exists, assessable profits are commonly deemed to be 30% of gross royalties for certain IP categories, producing an effective statutory tax of approximately 4.95% for corporations and 4.5% for an unincorporated FIP; under the China-HK DTA, interest is generally limited to 7% and royalties are generally limited to 7%, with dividends limited to 5% or 10% depending on beneficial ownership and direct shareholding thresholds

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: HK$10 million per controlled transaction category is the operative Hong Kong threshold for contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; a Local File and Master File must be prepared where controlled transactions exceed this threshold, and the Master File is additionally expected for MNE groups whose consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million; documentation must be ready for LRD inspection upon request and failure to maintain it shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer for arm s length pricing
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong does not have UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but its territorial source rule is effectively an economic substance doctrine: to claim offshore profits on matcha distribution, the FIP must prove that core income-generating activities (CIGA), including procurement decisions, contract negotiation, quality inspection, order acceptance, invoicing, banking, and risk bearing, are carried out by its own staff, premises, and systems in Hong Kong. A letter-box entity without substance will have its offshore-source claim denied and the entire trading profit may be assessed in Hong Kong; treaty benefits are also denied where the partnership is a pure conduit without economic substance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Material Misstatement of Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting matcha powder sales from BIR52, inflating intercompany purchasing costs from related Chinese suppliers, creating back-to-back sham invoices, or falsely claiming offshore source status for trading functions actually performed in Hong Kong
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Contravenes Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap.112) sections 59, 61, 61A, 80(2), 82 and 82A; civil additional tax up to treble the undercharged tax plus a penal fine of up to HK$100,000; on indictment, imprisonment for up to three years and fines up to HK$50,000; the LRD may reopen up to 10 years of assessment and issue an estimated assessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the commercial veil where the partnership is an instrument of tax evasion; partners and shadow directors may be personally liable for restitution of evaded tax, interest, and penal costs; the LRD may invoke the Hong Kong blacklisting/travel restriction regime for unpaid tax above HK$5,000, disqualify directors under the Companies Ordinance, and obtain a custody/imprisonment order for up to three years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Conduit Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Hong Kong FIP as a no-substance conduit between mainland Chinese matcha producers and overseas buyers solely to obtain offshore trading exemption or to access China-HK DTA benefits, with no office, staff, telecommunications records, business decisions, board oversight, or other evidence of core income-generating activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The LRD may void the arrangement under section 61A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance and recharacterise income as assessable in Hong Kong; transfer pricing adjustments under sections 50AAF and 50AAI add back non-arm s length profits; statutory penalties reach up to 100% of the additional tax and the DTA claim is denied under the Principal Purpose Test; a sham company may be struck off and its transactions disregarded for tax purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling partners face civil liability for wrongful trading and fraudulent misrepresentation; asset restitution orders may freeze bank accounts in Hong Kong, China, and treaty states; travel bans may be imposed pending investigation; director disqualification for up to 15 years is available under sections 168E and 168M of the Companies Ordinance; criminal liability for conspiracy to defraud the revenue may result in imprisonment of up to 14 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify the true beneficial owner of the FIP while moving SWIFT/TT and wire transfer proceeds from matcha sales through Hong Kong bank accounts, using nominee partners to conceal the Chinese revenue owner, accepting cash or third-party settlement without a Commercial Relationships, or misleading the bank and the Companies Registry in beneficial ownership declarations; a false declaration enables tax evasion by another person and creates a money-laundering predicate offence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap.615), sections 5 and 6, and the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap.455), section 25; corporate penalties may reach HK$5,000,000 and imprisonment for individuals up to 14 years; false beneficial ownership declarations attract separate offences under the Companies Ordinance and the AMLO with fines and imprisonment of up to seven years; the PIU may freeze and forfeit all matcha distribution proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge, recklessness, or wilful blindness to the disguised beneficial owner are personally criminally liable; civil asset restitution and confiscation orders can reach personal bank accounts and real estate; the director may be blacklisted by the Customs and Excise Department and travel-ban denied; the corporate veil is pierced where the director assists dishonest conduct, and imprisonment terms up to 14 years may be imposed for laundering proceeds of unlawful tax evasion and for conspiracy to defraud
